name: 'On the more correct view' (ʿalā al-aṣaḥḥ)
definition: A phrase of preference: of two or more views, each with some support, the author takes the one he holds more correct.
body: The handbooks weigh views with a fixed set of words. Al-aṣaḥḥ, 'the more correct', prefers one sound view to another; al-ṣaḥīḥ, 'the correct', sets a view against one the author holds unsound; al-rājiḥ and al-marjūḥ are the stronger and the weaker; al-mukhtār is the author's own choice. 'It was said' (qīla) before a view usually marks it as weak, and 'he claimed' (zaʿama) as one the author rejects.
Al-Suyūṭī's Hamʿ al-hawāmiʿ and Ibn Mālik's al-Tashīl use these terms with care, and the commentators argue over which a given author meant.

examples.text: 'And it was said': a weaker view follows.
